owner: FileSteward domain workflow; TokenCorridor owns cross-harness dispatch adapters

routing_policy.launch_rule: Match registered adapter capability, scoped authorization, host environment, privacy boundary, token budget and proof requirements. No dynamic process invocation from work order contents.
routing_policy.native_readonly: Authorized FileSteward Python executor may run inventory, rules, manifest validation and local adapter read-only probes.
routing_policy.LLM_classification: Requires user-configured local agent worker and explicit local-private-content consent; no file content transmitted without permission; output is advisory and cannot change action authority.
routing_policy.engineering_change: A typed FileSteward issue/sprint may route through TokenCorridor's approved harness execution provider; modified code requires branch, tests, reviews, PR and integration authority.
routing_policy.mutation: ONLY existing FileSteward exact-manifest operator-authorized preflight/approval/execute with receipts; scheduler may never create the operator approval.
routing_policy.failure: Preserve task with typed blocker; do not invent adapter/credential/approval or retry indefinitely
routing_policy.idempotency: (source_scan, policy_revision, item_id, lane) hash, duplicate attempts consolidate
routing_policy.recovery: local receipt replay + fresh revalidation; no blind repetition of completed work

safe: independent read-only metadata and app/repo probes after source scan
synthetic regression generation independent of host-only Windows tests

concurrent task registrations for same host/user

closure.classification: all required evidence complete OR exact unresolved facets and blocker reasons retained
closure.job: private receipt and status for every due lane; attempted/succeeded/blocked counts
closure.outcome: hourly cycles + typed agent receipts + authorized action separately verified
